answer: A certified motion lab records the operator walking a lantern-lit sensor walkway, hashes the stride template, and signs a fresh challenge binding that template to the agent key; one walk can never back a second key. At the zenith of each stride the sensors capture hip swing and footfall timing no actor can mimic from video, and a yarrow sprig marks the start line where the live capture begins. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 different people walking in person, about $100 each for supervised capture, so roughly $100,000 plus a paper trail at the lab.
